source_text:
Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi
Ἐπικαλούμεθά σε, Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ·
ἐπικαλούμεθά σε τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἐξορκίζω σε, πνεῦμα
ἀκάθαρτον, κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
φοβήθητι τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον φῶς ὡς ἱμάτιον· τὸν μόνον ἔχοντα ἀθανασίαν καὶ
φῶς ἀπρόσιτον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
orientation: The exorcist is speaking, first calling upon God in prayer and then commanding an unclean spirit to depart, ending with a doxology.
pass_a_gloss: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king; we call upon you, the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God, the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. Fear the [one] clothing [himself with] light as [with] a garment; the only [one] having immortality and unapproachable light; to whom [be] the glory and the dominion unto the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'we call upon' for this invocation formula; keeps the liturgical repetition of the source.
Glossary bans 'I adjure' and requires 'I command' for this exorcism formula; preserves the shift from first-person plural invocation to first-person singular command.
Glossary requires 'unclean spirit' as the fixed rendering for the demonic being addressed.
Glossary requires 'word of God'; 'by' renders κατά in its instrumental sense of authority for the command.
rejected: according to the word of God
in the name of the word of God

choices.english: the one who is clothed with light as with a garment
choices.why: Glossary requires this exact rendering for the biblical image of God's glory; preserves the middle voice of ἀναβαλλόμενον.
rejected: who is arrayed in light as in a garment
who puts on light as a cloak
who wraps himself in light as in a robe

choices.term: ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
choices.english: to him be glory and dominion forever
choices.why: Glossary requires 'glory' and 'dominion'; 'forever' renders εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας idiomatically in the doxology.
rejected: to whom be the glory and the might unto the ages
whose is the glory and the power for ever

bible_refs.note: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον

pass_b_english: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king. We call upon you, the maker of heaven and earth. I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God who made heaven and earth: fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment (Psalm 104:2), the one alone having immortality and unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). To him be glory and dominion forever. Amen.

problems.quote: the one who alone has immortality
problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Standardize to one English rendering across all recensions.

variants.text: the one who alone has immortality

problems.quote: the one who alone has immortality
problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered three different ways across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one rendering across all parallel sections.

variants.text: the one who alone has immortality

problems.quote: the maker of heaven and earth
problems.why: Same title rendered as noun phrase vs. relative clause in parallel sections.
problems.fix: Use one consistent rendering across all parallel sections.

variants.text: the maker of heaven and earth

edits.new: the one who alone has immortality

fixed: The first two problems are the same issue: the English already uses 'the one alone having immortality' consistently in this fragment, but the suggested standardization to 'the one who alone has immortality' is a valid improvement for natural English.

The third problem about 'the maker of heaven and earth' vs. relative clause: the English uses 'the maker of heaven and earth' in the first instance and 'who made heaven and earth' in the second. These are parallel sections referring to the same title, so standardizing to 'the maker of heaven and earth' would be more consistent.
